text: Fill in the missing terms about haemoglobin variants and pathological derivatives.
questions: In sickle cell disease, *valine* replaces glutamate at position 6 of the beta chain, enabling polymerisation of deoxygenated HbS.
Carriers of the sickle cell trait have a selective advantage because they resist falciparum *malaria*.
Carbon monoxide binds haem about 200 times more tightly than oxygen, forming *carboxyhaemoglobin/HbCO* which fools the pulse oximeter.
In beta-thalassaemia trait, the diagnostic finding on haemoglobin HPLC is a raised *HbA2*.
Methaemoglobin contains oxidised *ferric/Fe3+* iron that cannot carry oxygen and is normally reduced by NADH-methaemoglobin reductase.

overallFeedback.feedback: HbS results from a single valine-for-glutamate substitution causing sickling under deoxygenation; carriers resist falciparum malaria, explaining the gene's persistence in endemic regions; carboxyhaemoglobin fools pulse oximetry because it absorbs light like oxyhaemoglobin; raised HbA2 is the hallmark of beta-thalassaemia trait; and ferric iron in methaemoglobin cannot bind oxygen.
